questions.question: According to USP <1228>, how is "depyrogenation" defined in this series of chapters, and what does it refer to?

options.A: Killing all microorganisms in a product by moist heat sterilization and confirming the result by sterility testing; in this series it specifically refers to spores
options.B: The direct and validated destruction or removal of pyrogens; in this series it specifically refers to bacterial endotoxin
options.C: Removing particulates from a product by filtration and confirming it by particle counting; in this series it specifically refers to insoluble foreign matter
options.D: Monitoring the endotoxin content of raw materials and water systems; in this series it specifically refers to indirect control measures

questions.explanation: Depyrogenation is the direct and validated destruction or removal of pyrogens, and this series focuses on bacterial endotoxin because it is the most common and quantifiable pyrogen in injectable products. The option "Monitoring the endotoxin content of raw materials and water systems" is an indirect or process control, not depyrogenation itself.

questions.question: LPS consists of three regions. Which one contributes most to the biological activity of endotoxin and is the most conserved among Gram-negative bacteria?

options.A: O-antigen, which is hydrophilic and highly variable
options.B: Core oligosaccharide, the core sugar chain linking the two ends
options.C: O-specific side chain, which distinguishes the serological specificity of strains

questions.explanation: The hydrophobic lipid A is highly conserved among Gram-negative bacteria and is responsible for almost all of the biological activity of endotoxin. The O-antigen, by contrast, is highly variable, confers serological specificity and is often used to distinguish strains, so it is not the main source of activity.
questions.reference: USP <1228> Bacterial Endotoxin and Lipopolysaccharide (three LPS regions, item 1)

questions.question: Purified LPS (such as RSE and CSE) readily forms configurations such as micelles in solution and may adsorb to surfaces, making it difficult to extract and detect. What is the main reason?

options.A: The LPS molecule has both a hydrophilic end and a hydrophobic end (amphipathic)
options.B: The LPS molecule is only hydrophilic, so it dissociates completely in solution and does not aggregate
options.C: After purification LPS loses its lipid A, becomes an inactive molecule and precipitates
options.D: LPS is identical to native endotoxin, so it adsorbs to the surfaces of all materials

questions.explanation: The amphipathic nature of LPS causes it to form bilayers, micelles, ribbons and other configurations in solution and to adsorb to surfaces. The degree of adsorption is also affected by material composition and surface treatment, and aggregation in solution is affected by temperature, pH, salt concentration, divalent cations, surfactants and chelating agents.
questions.reference: USP <1228> Bacterial Endotoxin and Lipopolysaccharide (amphipathic LPS, adsorption)

questions.question: A depyrogenation study of a product stream aims to make the challenge material closer to actual contamination. According to <1228>, which is more appropriate?

options.A: Use only purified LPS, because purified LPS and native endotoxin are interchangeable and need not be compared
options.B: Use a higher concentration of purified LPS to compensate for adsorption loss and make the challenge more difficult
options.C: Consider using native endotoxin, because the actual contaminant is cells or cell wall fragments with LPS embedded in them
options.D: There is no need to consider the type of challenge material, because material and formulation do not affect aggregation, adsorption or recovery

questions.explanation: What actually contaminates injectable products is not purified LPS but whole cells or cell wall fragments in which the LPS is embedded. Native endotoxin better reflects real conditions and is less prone to the aggregation and adsorption problems of purified LPS. The document specifically notes that the two terms should not be used interchangeably.
questions.reference: USP <1228> Bacterial Endotoxin and Lipopolysaccharide (native endotoxin vs purified LPS)

questions.question: In the <1228> series, which statement about the use of the terms "challenge material", "endotoxin" and "LPS" is correct?

options.A: The three are fully synonymous and can be substituted freely in reports, with no need to define or explain them in the document
options.B: Challenge material generally means the endotoxin or LPS used for spiking; endotoxin is native cell wall fragments and LPS is the purified substance
options.C: Challenge material refers specifically to CSE; endotoxin refers specifically to RSE; LPS refers specifically to native contaminants
options.D: Challenge material refers specifically to native contaminants; endotoxin and LPS both refer to purified standards

questions.explanation: The document defines challenge material as the general term for the spiked material (endotoxin or LPS); endotoxin refers to cell wall fragments of Gram-negative bacteria from a well-characterized source in their native state; LPS refers to the purified substance. Treating endotoxin and LPS as the same thing is exactly what the document seeks to avoid.
questions.reference: USP <1228> Bacterial Endotoxin and Lipopolysaccharide (challenge material, endotoxin, LPS definitions)

questions.question: The 3-log reduction first proposed in 1984: under the concepts of QbD and risk management, how does <1228> view it as a universal benchmark?

options.A: It is still the minimum standard that every depyrogenation process must achieve, regardless of the starting endotoxin level
options.B: It applies only to filtration processes and not to dry heat processes, because dry heat processes use a different benchmark
options.C: It does not necessarily apply; a high-endotoxin fermentation broth may need more than 3 logs, while dry heat for washed low-endotoxin glass vials needs far less than 3 logs
options.D: It should always be changed to 6 logs, because a higher log reduction is safer for all processes regardless of load

questions.explanation: The document states that 3 logs may not be suitable as a universal benchmark for modern processes. The appropriate log reduction should be determined by the user according to the product and process capability, including the input source, endotoxin level, method efficiency and output requirements, rather than applying a fixed number.
questions.reference: USP <1228> Measuring Endotoxin Pre- and Post-Processing, point 7

questions.question: A product stream normally contains <1 EU of endotoxin in that volume. If, following the "industry standard", it is spiked so that at least 1000 EU of CSE can be recovered, what is the document's view?

options.A: It may be excessive; it should be adjusted according to system conditions, and the logic and rationale should be documented
options.B: It is insufficient; the spike should be increased to 10,000 EU or more to ensure a sufficient challenge
options.C: It is exactly right, because 1000 EU is a mandatory fixed value that need not be adjusted
options.D: No justification is needed, because 1000 EU is an industry standard and does not need to be documented

questions.explanation: The industry standard is to recover at least 1000 EU, but depending on the test system this amount may be too much or too little; in this example the product stream is normally <1 EU, so spiking 1000 EU may be excessive. The document requires that the logic and methodology of endotoxin reduction studies be scientifically justified and documented.
questions.reference: USP <1228> Measuring Endotoxin Pre- and Post-Processing, point 3

questions.question: In a depyrogenation study, when the recovery of the positive control is below the nominal spiked value (<100%), what does the document consider most important?

options.A: Recovery must reach 100%, otherwise the study is invalid
options.B: Switch to a different brand of BET reagent until recovery reaches 100%
options.C: As long as no endotoxin is detected in the processed sample, recovery need not be evaluated or recorded
options.D: Recovery should be consistent between different lots of the same material and between different studies

questions.explanation: The document notes that recovery below 100% is not unusual, and that there is no standard recovery method when a solid surface is used as the indicator. More important than the recovery percentage of a single test is consistency across lots and across studies. Requiring 100% recovery is not the document's position.
questions.reference: USP <1228> Measuring Endotoxin Pre- and Post-Processing, point 5

questions.question: <1228> divides endotoxin control into three categories. Which category is "monitoring endotoxin at critical control points (CCPs) to ensure that endotoxin does not increase during the process"?

options.A: Indirect control, including preventive measures for raw materials, water and environment
options.C: Direct control, directly destroying or removing endotoxin
options.D: Routine testing, regarded as the main control mechanism

questions.explanation: Process control is monitoring endotoxin at CCPs to ensure it does not increase, and these control elements need to be validated or verified. Indirect control is preventive bioburden management; direct control is what directly destroys or removes endotoxin. The document also states clearly that testing itself is not a control mechanism.
questions.reference: USP <1228> Control of Endotoxin in Parenteral Products (process control)

questions.topic: Process control — hold times and cleaning
questions.question: A site finds that the in-process holding time of non-sterile bulk is often extended. According to the process control concept in <1228>, what is the most appropriate action?

options.A: As long as the final product is tested for endotoxin, there is no need to specifically validate or manage bulk holding time
options.B: Extend the dry heat time and raise the dry heat temperature instead of managing holding time
options.C: Validate the hold time to ensure that the holding conditions do not support microbial proliferation and endotoxin generation
options.D: Shorten equipment cleaning time and keep cleaned equipment wet to facilitate the next batch

questions.explanation: The document requires that in-process hold times, especially for non-sterile bulk and drug products, be validated to ensure the conditions do not support the proliferation of Gram-negative bacteria and potential endotoxin generation. Cleaned product-contact equipment should be stored dry and cleaning procedures should emphasize removal of standing water, so keeping equipment wet is the opposite of this.

questions.question: When selecting a depyrogenation method (dry heat, chemical, filtration, physical removal), what is the document's principle?

options.A: Strike a compromise between the conditions for endotoxin removal and the impact on the material, and do not be more aggressive than needed for effective control
options.B: Always choose the most aggressive conditions to ensure endotoxin is completely destroyed, and accept changes in material properties
options.C: Decide the method by equipment cost alone, without considering the effect on the material or evaluating endotoxin removal
options.D: As long as the method is widely used, there is no need to evaluate its effect on material quality attributes or to validate it

questions.explanation: Method selection is often a compromise between the conditions needed to reach the target endotoxin level and the impact on the material, so the process should not be more aggressive than needed for effective control, to avoid damaging the material's quality attributes. A good understanding of depyrogenation technologies and their impact on materials is needed for selection.
questions.reference: USP <1228> Selection of an Appropriate Depyrogenation Method

questions.question: In the validation stages of depyrogenation, what is the purpose of OQ (operational qualification)?

options.A: Confirm that the instruments are correctly designed and calibrated and that utilities such as steam, water and air are acceptable
options.B: Directly evaluate the depyrogenation effect on materials or articles using actual or simulated product
options.C: Explore and establish the operating parameters that define process control
options.D: Confirm that the equipment and other process elements operate within the defined depyrogenation parameters

questions.explanation: OQ confirms that the equipment and other process elements can operate within the specified range of depyrogenation parameters. "Confirm that the instruments are correctly designed and calibrated" describes IQ, "directly evaluate using actual or simulated product" describes PQ, and "explore and establish the operating parameters that define process control" is the development stage; these are easily confused and must be distinguished by the purpose of each stage.
questions.reference: USP <1228> Validation of a Depyrogenation Method > OQ stage

questions.question: A site is performing PQ on dry heat depyrogenation of glass vials and must design worst-case conditions. According to <1228>, which is most appropriate?

options.A: Use only the most favorable time and temperature combination so that it passes easily, with no need to explain this in the protocol
options.B: Bracket key parameters such as time/temperature and conveyor speed, and explain the worst case in the protocol
options.C: Use a single parameter with no bracketing, because the worst case needs no justification and no documentation
options.D: Avoid using actual or simulated product to prevent contamination, and complete all validation batches with empty vials

questions.explanation: PQ should use or simulate actual use conditions as far as possible, including real or simulated product. The worst case for dry heat of glass vials can include bracketing of time/temperature and conveyor speed, and for filtration can include flow rate, and should cover the maximum endotoxin load. The worst case must be defined and justified in the validation protocol.
questions.reference: USP <1228> Validation of a Depyrogenation Method > PQ stage (worst case)

questions.question: What is <1228>'s view on the "rule of three" (three consecutive successful validation runs)?

options.A: Three is the absolute minimum and maximum number required by regulation; no more and no fewer, with no exceptions
options.B: Once three consecutive runs pass, there is no need to verify the equipment's operating range, worst-case conditions or process robustness again
options.C: Enough replicate studies should be performed on a scientific basis to demonstrate process capability; the number needs a scientific rationale and an explanation
options.D: After three passing runs, there is no need to write a PQ report or obtain approval from the responsible unit

questions.explanation: Although the document mentions that the rule of three suggests three consecutive successes, it stresses that enough replicate studies should be performed to demonstrate the capability and efficiency of the process, including verification of the equipment operating range, and that the number must have a scientific basis. A report must still be written after PQ to establish the operating parameters.
questions.reference: USP <1228> Validation of a Depyrogenation Method > PQ stage (rule of three)

questions.question: Which statement about routine testing for depyrogenation in <1228> is correct?

options.A: Testing is not a control mechanism but a tool for evaluating the effectiveness of control measures
options.B: Testing is the only control mechanism and can therefore replace process control
options.C: Testing limits should be completely independent of historical data and determined by the current result
options.D: Testing of raw materials and water is not needed in a validated process

questions.explanation: The document states clearly that testing is not a control mechanism but a tool used to evaluate the effectiveness of control measures. Testing of raw materials, water and in-process samples uses limits set from historical data to ensure that the finished product reaches an acceptable endotoxin level and to help maintain the validated state.
